title: Lender provides £774,000 for Yorkshire hotel acquisition
summary:
A specialist lender has provided £774,000 in bridging finance for the acquisition of a mixed-use seafront property in East Yorkshire, completing the transaction in under two months. The 18-month facility was advanced at 90% loan-to-value against a purchase price of £860,000.

title: Shawbrook completes £271k bridging loan in 10 days
summary:
Shawbrook Bank has completed a £271,000 bridging loan for Vitae Investments Ltd, releasing equity from a property in Bexhill-on-Sea. The transaction was completed within 10 working days of agreement in principle, three days ahead of the borrower's deadline.

title: Smart locks for UK homes: costs, installation and insurance
summary:
A growing number of UK homeowners are installing smart locks on their front doors, but industry experts warn that buyers must carefully consider compatibility, insurance requirements and professional installation to avoid invalidating home cover. Smart locks allow entry without traditional keys, using methods including codes, smartphones, fingerprints, voice assistants or facial recognition.

title: Three lettings firms merge under new group structure
summary:
Propoly, LegalforLandlords and Landlord Lounge have merged under the Rental Intelligence Group to streamline lettings administration. The group plans to integrate services and introduce AI automation, though specific timelines and cost savings remain unquantified.

The post Three lettings firms merge under new group structure appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Building safety crisis drains leaseholder finances
summary:
Leaseholders continue to deplete their savings whilst awaiting resolution of the building safety crisis, according to campaigners, despite new government measures introduced to Parliament aimed at expanding financial protections. More than nine years after the Grenfell Tower fire, many leaseholders remain liable for remediation costs for defects they did not cause.

The post Building safety crisis drains leaseholder finances appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: eXp UK reduces commission cap for high-producing teams
summary:
eXp UK has announced changes to its commission structure, reducing the cap for qualifying estate agency teams by £6,000 as part of a new tiered model launching on 1 November 2026. The self-employed estate agency network will introduce a Premier Teams structure alongside its existing Standard Teams arrangement.

The post eXp UK reduces commission cap for high-producing teams appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Bank of England poised for rate rise amid inflation jump
summary:
The Bank of England is expected to raise the base interest rate by 0.25 percentage points on Thursday, with market traders pricing in a near-96% probability of an increase. The anticipated move follows a recent jump in inflation to 3.5%.

The post Bank of England poised for rate rise amid inflation jump appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK house prices forecast to rise 1.5% in 2027
summary:
House prices across Britain are expected to rise by 1.5% in 2027, with modest growth continuing through 2029, according to forecasts from Connells Group. The estate agency network projects prices will increase by 1% in 2026, followed by 1.5% in 2027, 2.5% in 2028, and 2% in 2029.

title: Tribunal hears £1.5bn group claim against Rightmove
summary:
The Competition Appeal Tribunal is hearing arguments on whether a £1.5 billion legal action against Rightmove can proceed as a collective claim on behalf of thousands of estate agents. The case alleges that Rightmove abused its dominant market position by charging excessive and unfair fees.

The post Tribunal hears £1.5bn group claim against Rightmove appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Property tax reform needed to address housing crisis
summary:
The UK's housing system has been described as "one of the most dysfunctional in the world" by Oxford academic John Muellbauer, who argues that fundamental tax reform is necessary to address chronic affordability issues. Proposals include remodelling council tax into an annual levy whilst abolishing stamp duty on transactions.
